# About the author {.unnumbered}

**Umar Ahmad, PhD**, is Senior Lecturer in the Department of Anatomy and the Human Genetics
Informatics Unit, Faculty of Basic Medical Sciences, Sa'adu Zungur University, Bauchi,
Nigeria, and Senior Technical Officer for Pathogen Genomics at the Africa Centres for
Disease Control and Prevention. He took his PhD in human genetics and genomics at
Universiti Putra Malaysia and the Malaysia Genome Institute, and has worked for more
than twelve years across genomics research, bioinformatics and multi-country scientific
collaboration in Africa.

His research is in cancer genomics: transcriptome profiling of bladder and other
urothelial cancers, using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, whole-genome and whole-exome
sequencing to identify molecular drivers, therapeutic resistance and protein interaction
networks, and the mechanisms by which oncolytic Newcastle disease virus establishes
persistent infection in cancer cells.

At Africa CDC he coordinates genomic surveillance, bioinformatics and workforce
development across African Union Member States, and leads AGARI, the continental
platform for pathogen genomic data sharing and public health intelligence. He has
contributed to genomic surveillance strategies at both continental and national level,
among them the Pathogen Genomic Surveillance Policy Framework, the roadmap for malaria
genomic surveillance in Africa, the AC-GCAT genomics capacity assessment tool and its
manual, and continental technical guidance on mpox testing and sequencing.

In 2021 he founded BioSeq, a genomics and bioinformatics company built on four pillars:
genomics, bioinformatics, artificial intelligence and capacity building. He also founded
the Open Science Community Nigeria, which has since grown into the Open Science
Community Network. He is an Academic Editor of PLOS ONE and of Applied Research, a
member of the Bioconductor Community Advisory Board, a board member of the Directory of
Open Access Journals and of the International Network of Open Science and Scholarship
Communities, and a founding member both of the Nigerian Bioinformatics and Genomics
Network and of the Community of Practice on Human Genomics and Genomic Medicine at the
Africa Bioinformatics Institute.

He teaches human genetics, bioinformatics and R programming, supervises postgraduate
research, and has designed genomics and bioinformatics training for professionals across
the continent. This book is a direct expression of the conviction that computational
skills are learned by use.
